# Verified Catalog: Interpretability / Probing / Diagnostics for VLAs, Robot Policies, and World Models

**Method note:** `WebFetch` is blocked for arxiv.org and api.semanticscholar.org in this environment; all verification was done via Bash `curl`. Every arXiv ID below was fetched from its `/abs/` page and the title compared against the claim. Venue comes from the arXiv **Comments** field verbatim (empty = no venue stated on arXiv, which is *not* evidence of rejection). Citations via the Semantic Scholar **batch** endpoint (the single-paper endpoint is rate-limited to uselessness; batch works with ~45s spacing). WebSearch budget hit its 200-call cap partway, so later discovery used the arXiv HTML search UI and the OpenReview search API via curl.

## Verdict on your 8 flagged IDs: all 8 are REAL. Zero hallucinations.

But **two of your descriptions were wrong**:

- **2602.04880** — you described it as "ICLR 2026 probing visual encoders / state decoding." Real title: **"Capturing Visual Environment Structure Correlates with Control Performance."** The subject matter is right (it does probe visual encoders for state decoding), but the Comments field is **empty** — there is no ICLR 2026 acceptance stated on arXiv. Don't cite it as ICLR 2026.
- **2603.21546** — real, but much smaller than the title suggests: Comments say *"5 pages, 3 figures, 1 table"* and it's a **single-author** note (Xinyu Zhang). Workshop-scale, not a full paper.

## Grouped by analysis method

### SAE / dictionary learning
| ID | Title | Venue (Comments verbatim) | Cites | Compute |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2603.19183 | Sparse Autoencoders Reveal Interpretable and Steerable Features in VLA Models | "24 pages, 11 figures" | 11 | Trains SAEs only, base VLA frozen; LIBERO + **real DROID hardware** |
| 2605.17204 | Event-Grounded Sparse Autoencoders for Vision-Language-Action Policies | — | 0 | **LOW**: "a few GPU-hours per BatchTopK SAE on a single A100; each LIBERO rollout ~1–2 min on a single GPU" |
| 2603.19233 | Not All Features Are Created Equal: A Mechanistic Study of VLA Models | "Accepted to Multimodal Intelligence Workshop @ ICLR" | 9 | Frozen ckpts + SAE training; "8×A100-SXM4-80GB cluster, an RTX 5090, and two RTX 4090s" — **SmolVLA/X-VLA work done on 4090s** |

Method: BatchTopK SAEs on residual stream; 2605.17204's twist is ranking features against clustered end-effector *keyframe events* rather than activation statistics; 2603.19233 spans six VLAs (80M–7B) over 394k rollout episodes.

**Critical counterpoint — the negative result.** "When Internal Feedback Goodharts: SAE Rewards Fail to Improve Robot Success," **ICML 2026 RLxF Workshop**, `openreview.net/forum?id=h0uehSJqbm`. No arXiv version found. On Octo-Base/SimplerEnv, SAE features show task/phase structure and are *optimizable*, yet SAE-feature reranking succeeds in only 1 of 4 episodes where native Octo succeeds 4/4 — matching random-chunk and random-feature controls. Their framing is the "proxy–success gap": sparse features can be valid diagnostics and optimizable proxies while still failing as control signal. This is the single most useful cautionary cite in the set.

Also OpenReview-only: "Controlling Vision–Language–Action Policies through Sparse Latent Directions," **Mech Interp Workshop (NeurIPS 2025) Poster**, `forum?id=wtf3ww1EOL`. SAE on a Magma-style ConvNeXt + LLaMA-3-8B decoder residual stream in SimplerEnv.

### Activation steering / causal intervention
- **2509.00328** — *Mechanistic interpretability for steering vision-language-action models*. Comments: **"CoRL 2025.** Project website: this https URL". **27 cites** — the most-cited dedicated VLA mech-interp paper. Logit-lens-style projection of FFN value vectors onto the token embedding basis → sparse semantic directions (speed, direction) → inference-time steering. **Frozen π0 + OpenVLA, no fine-tuning, no reward, no env interaction**; LIBERO + physical UR5. Headline finding: internal activity stays largely *semantic*, with &lt;25% of FFN neurons rewired for action prediction.
- **2603.05487** — *Observing and Controlling Features in Vision-Language-Action Models*. 12 cites. Feature-*observability* (linear classifier) + feature-*controllability* (minimal linear intervention grounded in optimal control) on π0.5 + OpenVLA. **LOW COMPUTE, explicit: "All inference is done using a single NVIDIA 5090 GPU."**
- **2605.00321** — *Embodied Interpretability...*. Comments: **"Accepted at the 43rd International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML 2026)"**. 2 cites. Interventional Significance Score + Nuisance Mass Ratio. **Caveat: intervenes on visual *inputs* (masking/noise), not activations** — despite the framing, this is not activation patching.
- **2605.24322** — *Causal Physics Steering in Video World Models via Concept Activation Vectors*. Comments: **"In proceedings of CVPR 2026 workshop on Video World Model"**. 3 cites. Uses a linear probe's weight vector at a "Physics Emergence Zone" layer as a CAV, injected at inference. **Training-free on frozen VideoMAE.**

### Linear probing of VLAs
- **2502.04558** — *Probing a VLA Model for Symbolic States...*. 14 cites (S2 venue field says "International Conference on Auditory Display" — almost certainly an indexing artifact; the authors' lab lists it as ICAD'25). Multi-label linear probes across **all 33** OpenVLA Llama-2-7B layers, 224 object atoms + 12 action atoms. &gt;0.90 accuracy layers 1–32; **layer 0 only 0.57–0.71**. Frozen OpenVLA, probes only, ran live at **5–10 Hz**.
- **2509.24559** — *Emergent World Representations in OpenVLA*. 5 cites. Lasso linear + MLP probes predicting **state-transition vectors** (not static state) from layers 7/15/22/30, with permutation tests and a crucial activation-vs-raw-embedding baseline. Frozen OpenVLA-7B, 400 episodes / 66,931 steps.
- **2608.13474** — *Decoding Task Progress from VLA Representations*. 0 cites. Task progress linearly readable from π0.5 residual stream; **present in pretrained PaliGemma before any robot data**; generalizes to unseen tasks; **explicitly does NOT enable steering**; works as label-free OOD detector. Probes are cheap but they trained π0.5 ckpts on **eight H100 GPUs**.
- **2605.28527** — *What Frozen VLAs Already Know About Success*. Comments: "14 pages, 1 figure, 11 tables... Preprint". 0 cites. Probes frozen OpenVLA/π0.5/DINOv2/CLIP for Monte-Carlo *value* targets, with same-task/same-timestep matched controls and label-shuffled controls. **LOW COMPUTE, explicit: "Probes train in under five minutes on a single GPU."**
- **2608.07361** — *Depth-Wise Probing and Pruning of the Planning Token in a Driving VLA*. Comments: **"Accepted at the 6th DriveX Workshop (Foundation Models for Autonomous Driving), ECCV 2026"**. 0 cites. **Trajectory-space logit lens** — decodes the single planning token from all 32 layers using the frozen native planner as readout. Command probe hits 97.7% after layer 1 (chance 16.7%), but Avg-L2 bottoms at 2.11 m only at the final layer.

### Attention analysis
- **2606.09749** — *Your Model Already Knows: Attention-Guided Safety Filter for VLAs*. Comments: "Under review". 0 cites. A small set of attention heads reliably localizes the policy's intended target object; feeds a CBF-QP filter. **Training-free on a frozen VLA, "no additional training or supervision."**
- **2605.30117** — *VLA-Trace: Diagnosing VLA Models through Representation and Behavior Tracing*. 2 cites. Three-stage: cross-modal + checkpoint-drift **CKA**, **attention-knockout** interventions, and rollout behavioral probes. On π0.5 + OpenVLA. Finds the two models use different multimodal routing strategies, and that both excel at visually grounded trajectories but remain limited at fine-grained semantic following.
- **2609.02634** — *Latent Cluster Analysis for Vision-Language-Action Models* (LAVLA). 0 cites. Layer-wise latent clustering of **GR00T N1.5**'s action decoder with cross-attention embedding weighting. Frozen-checkpoint analysis.
- **2608.20763** — *CARD: Diagnosing Belief to Action Routing Failures in VLMs*. 0 cites. Steers along one axis (belief) while measuring a *different* axis's prediction (action) — finds models fail to route belief representations into next-action prediction. VLM not VLA, but the cross-axis routing design is directly transferable.

### Behavioral diagnostics / robustness
- **2510.13626** — *LIBERO-Plus*. **233 cites**. Seven perturbation dimensions. Key finding for the "does the policy use language" question: performance falls 95% → below 30% under modest camera-viewpoint or robot-init perturbation, while models are *largely insensitive to language* and "tend to ignore language instructions completely." **NOT low-compute — they trained: 8×A100 for 150K steps, and 8×H100 for ~three weeks (4000 GPU hours).**
- **2510.03827** — *LIBERO-PRO*. **124 cites**. 90%+ collapses to **0.0%**; models keep grasping when the target is replaced by irrelevant objects, and outputs are unchanged under corrupted instructions or "messy tokens." Eval-centric on existing checkpoints.
- **2505.03500** — *VLAs are Confined yet Capable of Generalizing to Novel Instructions*. 8 cites, single author. Identifies a "text latent" (mean of text-token hidden states) and temporally interpolates it at inference. New `libero-ood` benchmark: SOTA VLAs &lt;15%, π0 + interpolation reaches 83%. Inference-time manipulation of a frozen π0.
- **2606.30686** — *Position: VLAs Cannot Be Verified to Perform Physical Reasoning*. 0 cites. Decomposes VLA into semantic mapping vs. physical action decision, argues success rate cannot distinguish them ("identifiability gap," "narrative drift"). No training. The closest thing to a position paper in this space.
- **2607.04681** — *Do VLAs Mean What They Say? On the Role of Faithfulness in Embodied Reasoning*. 0 cites. Separates *functional* from *faithful* reasoning for Embodied CoT.
- **2606.19998** — *Tri-Info: Generalizable, Interpretable Failure Prediction for VLA Models via Information Theory*. 1 cite. Information-theoretic signals across six VLAs and three benchmarks; transfers across architectures and sim-to-real **without retraining**, 83% on real-world tasks.

### World models / latent dynamics
- **2602.07050** — *Interpreting Physics in Video World Models*. **11 cites**, the most-cited in this subgroup. Claims the "first interpretability study to directly examine physical representations inside large-scale video encoders": layerwise probing, subspace geometry, patch-level decoding, targeted **attention ablations**. Finds a sharp intermediate-depth **"Physics Emergence Zone"**; physics peaks just after it and *degrades toward output layers*. Frozen encoders. (2605.24322 above is the steering follow-up.)
- **2606.07687** — *What Makes Video World Model Latents Action-Relevant: Prediction over Reconstruction*. 4 cites. Unified **inverse-dynamics probing** across encoder families. Finding: action-relevant structure comes from *temporal video pretraining, not pixel reconstruction fidelity* — models with strong pixel decoding can have near-zero action recoverability. CALVIN's static environments partially mask this. Probing frozen encoders.
- **2603.21546** — *What Do World Models Learn in RL?* 5 cites, 5 pages, single author. Linear + MLP probes, causal interventions along probe directions, attention-head analysis, token ablation — on **IRIS (discrete token transformer) vs DIAMOND (continuous diffusion UNet)** on Atari. Frozen checkpoints.
- **2602.04880** — *Capturing Visual Environment Structure Correlates with Control Performance*. 1 cite. Probes encoders for env-state decodability as a cheap proxy for expensive rollouts. **LOW COMPUTE, explicit: "using a single A100 GPU."**
- **2608.24885** — *Do Robotic World Models Really Follow Actions?* 0 cites. WorldEcho probes action-following over the **off-expert** action distribution via visual integrity + SE(3) trajectory alignment. Diagnosis: current world models handle expert actions but ignore commanded off-expert trajectories or produce visually invalid rollouts. Diagnosis is eval-only; the WorldSync fix trains.
- **2606.09028** — *ATM: Action-Consistency Transfer Matrix*. 2 cites. Lightweight **post-hoc** probes comparing action information in real vs. model-predicted transitions; replaces minutes-to-hours CEM planner eval with seconds-level analysis. **Low compute by design.**
- **2608.29998** — *The Intervention Gap in Latent World Models*. 0 cites. Matched-intervention audit on **released TD-MPC2 checkpoints** + LeWorldModel + PreJEPA seeds. Finds reward-prediction error stays small and flat while intervention fidelity degrades; failure is "task-direction rotation with excess gain, not feature collapse."
- **2607.06640** — *What a World Model Represents Is Three Questions*. 0 cites. Separates **reachability / admission / assignment**, and argues loss-ablation ("which route raises loss most if removed") does *not* identify the route the model actually uses. Methodologically important if you plan any ablation-based attribution.
- **2603.20327** — *Probing the Latent World: Emergent Discrete Symbols and Physical Structure*. 0 cites. Passive **quantization probe** turning V-JEPA 2 latents into discrete symbols, vocabulary-free, encoder completely frozen so structure is attributable to the encoder. Independent research report, low compute.
- **2606.09936** — *One Lens, Many Worlds: A Capability-Typed Interface for World-Model Interpretability*. 0 cites. **WorldModelLens** — open-source substrate unifying probing / activation patching / SAEs / surprise analysis across PlaNet, Dreamer, IRIS, I-JEPA. Tooling, no big training. Potentially the most practically useful item here.
- **2608.07077** — *Transformers Struggle to Use Their Emergent World Models* (Tower of Hanoi). 0 cites. Representation-vs-use gap.
- **2512.23722** — *Emergent World Beliefs: Exploring Transformers in Stochastic Games*. Comments: **"Accepted at NeurIPS 2025 Mechanistic Interpretability"**. 1 cite.

### Adjacent (verified, method-transferable but not core)
2603.13652 *Causal Attribution via Activation Patching* (2 cites, ViT-only — the cleanest transfer path for real activation patching into VLAs); 2603.23202 *Gaze-Regularized VLA* (4 cites, uses attention maps diagnostically but is primarily a training method); 2608.13422 *Attention from Action, for Action* (0 cites, Seeker, learns ROI from action supervision on frozen DINOv3); 2606.21496 *Decoupling the Declarative from the Procedural in VLAs* (0 cites, proposes w²VLA — a model, not an analysis); 2608.08273 *Action- and Language-Conditioned Video Assessment* (0 cites, ALVA evaluator).

## Two findings worth flagging

**The low-compute path is well-established.** Papers with explicit modest hardware: 2603.05487 (single RTX 5090), 2605.28527 (probes in &lt;5 min on one GPU), 2605.17204 (a few GPU-hours per SAE on one A100), 2602.04880 (single A100), 2603.19233 (SmolVLA/X-VLA on two RTX 4090s). Plus fully training-free work: 2509.00328, 2606.09749, 2605.24322, 2605.00321, 2603.20327. Frozen-checkpoint VLA interpretability is genuinely accessible — the expensive papers are the ones that *train* (2510.13626 at 4000 GPU-hours, 2608.13474 on 8×H100).

**A convergent, replicated result across independent groups:** VLAs largely ignore language and lean on the visual pathway. 2510.13626 ("tend to ignore language instructions completely"), 2510.03827 (outputs unchanged under corrupted instructions/messy tokens), 2603.19233 (cross-task visual activation injection dominates the prompt; language matters only when the scene doesn't uniquely specify the task), and 2605.30117 (fine-grained semantic following is the weak axis). That convergence from four independent methodologies is the strongest signal in this literature.

- **No arXiv ID exists** for the two OpenReview-only papers (both venue-confirmed via the OpenReview API instead): "When Internal Feedback Goodharts" (ICML 2026 RLxF Workshop) and "Controlling VLA Policies through Sparse Latent Directions" (NeurIPS 2025 MechInterp Workshop).
- **DR.VLA** (drvla.github.io) is the project page for 2603.19183, not a separate paper — search results imply otherwise.

- 2603.01879 *Diagnosing Generalization Failures from Representational Geometry Markers* (Comments: "Published in ICLR 2026") — title verified only; robotics relevance **unverified**.

## 但这一路也给了我最硬的坏消息，我照原样转给你

这一路挖到了**逐字核实的 OpenReview 评审文本**。结论跟我预期的不一样：

### 「没 SOTA」不是主要杀手。「结论不意外」才是。

| 精确短语 | OpenReview 全库命中 |
|---|---|
| `"findings are not particularly surprising"` | **9 次** |
| `"no closed-loop"` | **27 次**（ICLR 2026 集中） |
| `"no real-robot experiments"` | 18 次 |
| `"does not propose a new method"` | 17 次 |
| `"conclusions are not new"` | 4 次 |

最致命的一条，ICLR 2026 Sub 21082 逐字：

> **"Trivial and Unsurprising Findings**: The paper's primary conclusions are not new knowledge. The findings that later layers in a transformer are more task-specific… are foundational and well-documented"

**这正是纯逐层 probing 论文的标准死法。** 你 doc 06 那种"第 X 层能线性解码出 Y"的形态，单独拿出来会被这样打死。

而你的救命之处在于：**你做的不是描述性 probing，是因果干预**（固定噪声与 z、只换 `O^c`、比较动作变化幅度）。doc 09 里你自己写的那句话就是分界线：

> "前面都是 probe —— 只能说明「信息在不在」，不能说明「action head 用没用」。所以直接在 Stage-I 的 DiT 上做干预。"

**这个升级正是从"会被打死"到"能被接收"的那一步。** CoRL 2025 那篇（2509.00328，27 引用，已核实）和 CVPR 2026 workshop 那篇（2605.24322）走的都是这个配方：探针方向要能**反过来 training-free 地操控行为**。

### 第二个坏消息：offline-only 会被精确打击

逐字，ICLR 2026 Sub 13241：

> "Planning validation gap: no closed-loop or interactive evaluation; **critic-only and offline metrics don't establish** that predicted Δstates guide effective action sequences"

**而你的 PPU 无 Vulkan，正好切断了贵的那一半验证路径。** SimplerEnv 基于 SAPIEN，是唯一能在 fractal/bridge 上做闭环 rollout 的主流工具——你走不了。这意味着：

```
fractal/bridge（真实分布，你有数据）──► 只能 offline 分析
LIBERO/MuJoCo EGL（能闭环 rollout）──► 但不是 WoG 的训练分布
                        ↑
              这两头对不上，别假设能都占
```

**唯一合法出路**（有先例，2602.04880）：**把 offline 指标与下游性能的相关性本身做成贡献**，让 offline 指标成为被验证过的代理量，而不是当性能证据用。

### 第三件事：一个制度性利好

**TMLR 的接收标准逐字**：

> "it should not be used as a reason to reject work… **because it isn't achieving a new state-of-the-art on some benchmark**. Nor should it form the basis for rejecting work on a method considered not 'novel enough', as **novelty of the studied method is not a necessary criterion for acceptance in TMLR**."

而且明确写了：系统研究已有方法的鲁棒性/泛化性并给出 actionable lessons 的报告**可以被接收**。**这是正经期刊，不是 workshop。你的风险画像和 TMLR 的接收函数几乎完美匹配。**

# Analysis/Benchmark/Probing Papers in Robot Learning Peer Review: Evidence Dossier

## Tooling / methodology caveats (read first)

- **WebSearch budget was exhausted (200/200) before I made a single search call**, so I have **zero** Reddit/X/blog evidence. Section 2 of the task is a **hard gap**.
- **reddit.com is blocked for both WebFetch and curl** in this environment. `openreview.net` and `jmlr.org` are blocked for WebFetch (curl works).
- **OpenReview API is mostly walled off.** `/notes?forum=`, `/notes?id=`, `/notes?content.venueid=` all return `403 ChallengeRequiredError` on both api1 and api2, with or without a browser UA. Forum HTML is a JS shell with no embedded JSON. **The single working endpoint** is `https://api2.openreview.net/notes/search?term=&lt;urlencoded "quoted phrase"&gt;&amp;limit=N`, which returns full review content. All quotes below came through that channel. Unquoted multi-word terms return useless 10000-hit fuzzy results; **quoted exact phrases return true counts**.
- **arXiv API was rate-limiting/503-ing throughout**, so rather than risk fabricating IDs, I verified venues via DBLP records mirrored inside OpenReview. Where I have no arXiv ID, I say so. **I invented no IDs, quotes, or forum keys.**

## 1. Reviewer/AC statements penalizing analysis, sim-only, and offline-only work

### 1.1 The strongest single case study: offline-only metrics → ICLR reject → ICML accept

**"Scaling Laws for Pre-training Agents and World Models"** (Pearce, Rashid, Bignell, Georgescu, Devlin, Hofmann — Microsoft Research). An analysis-only world-model/imitation paper with **no robot, no closed-loop rollouts, only pre-training loss**.

- **[VERIFIED]** ICLR 2025: `venueid: ICLR.cc/2025/Conference/Rejected_Submission` — https://openreview.net/forum?id=D0XpSucS3l
- **[VERIFIED]** Reviewer weaknesses, verbatim, the two-punch combination of exactly the objections you asked about:
  &gt; "**Lack of real-world data:** The scaling insights are based on a single simulation task. Previous studies have demonstrated that simulation performance often does not correlate well with real-world robot performance [1]. The analysis would benefit from validation on openly available real-world datasets such as OpenX[2] and DROID[3]."
  &gt; "**Downstream task performance:** The paper focuses exclusively on scaling pre-training loss without examining generalization or performance on downstream tasks, which is crucial for embodied AI applications."
- **[VERIFIED]** Same reviewer's questions make the demand explicit: *"Would incorporating large-scale real-world robotics data help validate the paper's scaling law claims beyond simulation environments?"*
- **[VERIFIED]** The authors pushed back on offline-vs-online directly: *"we focus on pre-training loss rather than online performance, so it is unclear how relevant the findings are."* They also added OXE experiments during rebuttal. It was rejected anyway.
- **[VERIFIED]** Same paper, **accepted at ICML 2025 poster** — https://openreview.net/forum?id=HHwGfLOKxq (DBLP: `conf/icml/PearceRBGDH25`).

**This is your load-bearing data point: identical offline-only analysis paper, rejected at one top venue on "no real-world data / no downstream metrics," accepted at another months later.**

### 1.2 CoRL Area Chair decisions — real-robot experiments as an explicit acceptance condition

CoRL 2024 is the **last CoRL with public reviews** ([VERIFIED] — I checked venue-by-venue counts across the review corpus; CoRL 2025/2026 conference reviews do not appear in the search index at all, only submissions. Do not infer CoRL 2025+ norms from review text).

**CoRL 2024 Submission 631 — https://openreview.net/forum?id=s31IWg2kN5 (decision: Accept)** [VERIFIED]. An **Area Chair**, not a reviewer, conditioning acceptance on robot experiments and invoking venue scope:
&gt; "There are no real robot experiments or interesting robotics tasks beyond simple Mujoco benchmarks. Most reviewers agree that this is a major drawback, and I'll not vote for accepting this paper if a more convincing benchmark is presented, to match the scope of the CoRL conference."

Same decision also dinged novelty: *"The method seems to be not completely novel, and rather incremental."* Then: *"During the rebuttal ... the authors added a reasonable robotics experiment (the 3d quadrotor stabilization)."* → **the robotics-task demand was the binding constraint, and satisfying it flipped the outcome.**

**CoRL 2024 Submission 687 (PointFlowMatch) — https://openreview.net/forum?id=vtEn8NJWlz (Accept)** [VERIFIED]. Same mechanism, and notably the paper is framed as an **analysis/comparison** ("presents an investigation of conditional flow matching (CFM) versus diffusion policy", "architecture investigations"):
&gt; AC: "The primary issue is that the results are not strong enough with the performance only demonstrated through simulation on RLBench. There are no hardware experiments to validate the method in more complicated real-world scenarios."
&gt; AC: "During the rebuttal, the authors did an excellent job addressing the reviewers' concerns, particularly by including hardware results. As a result, all reviewers now rate the paper as a Weak Accept."
&gt; Reviewer: "Overall, I think this is a solid paper accomplishing what it sets out to do in terms of architecture investigations... **The only concern with this paper that I have is the lack of hardware experiments.**"

**CoRL 2024 Submission 437 — https://openreview.net/forum?id=DsFQg0G4Xu** [VERIFIED]. Absence of hardware moves the numeric score:
&gt; "However, due to no hardware experiments, my recommendation is 'weak accept'. Depending on responses to rebuttal questions, I could lean towards a 'strong accept' or a 'weak reject'."

**CoRL 2024 Submission 427 — https://openreview.net/forum?id=jPkOFAiOzf** [VERIFIED]. Review **titled** "Interesting idea, yet no real world experiments to support it"; recommendation explicitly grounded in them: *"My recommendation is based on real world experiments showing strength of the proposed approach."*

### 1.3 Offline-only / no-closed-loop attacks on world-model and VLA papers (ICLR 2026)

**ICLR 2026 Sub 13241, a Vision-Language World Model — https://openreview.net/forum?id=uvRApnkdbk** [VERIFIED]. Both objections in one review:
&gt; "**Planning validation gap: no closed-loop or interactive evaluation; critic-only and offline metrics don't establish that predicted Δstates guide effective action sequences** under uncertainty or partial observability."
&gt; "Methodological novelty is limited: most components ... are standard; the contribution is primarily pipeline integration rather than a new planning/world-model objective."

**ICLR 2026 Sub 11155, a VLA mechanistic-interpretability + benchmark paper (releases LIBERO-OOD) — https://openreview.net/forum?id=jtrhwfgseW** [VERIFIED]. Closest thing I found to a probing paper punished for sim-only:
&gt; "First and also most important: **All experiments are in simulation (LIBERO) — no real-robot validation.**"

Note the same reviewer credits it as *"First to identify and manipulate task-specific text latents inside VLAs"* — the interpretability contribution was recognized and the sim-only complaint was still ranked most important.

**ICLR 2026 Sub 5223 (Mitty, human→robot video) — https://openreview.net/forum?id=BxeJLOrKDF** [VERIFIED]:
&gt; "no real robot experiments are performed as there are no closed-loop policies. This leaves an important open question on whether visually good robot renderings can translate into accurate robot actions."

**ICLR 2026 Sub 9400 (UML-CoT embodied planning) — https://openreview.net/forum?id=nydRcDqjKL** [VERIFIED]:
&gt; "there is no closed-loop execution in simulators or on hardware, leaving executability claims supported only by text similarity proxies rather than task success."

**ICLR 2026 Sub 21401** — an **explicitly analysis-framed** human-intervention paper, https://openreview.net/forum?id=uEtTUMEipU [VERIFIED]. Reviewer concedes originality (*"The idea to analyze human interventions is novel"*) then:
&gt; "The baselines the method compares to all have real robot experiments to back up the methods, which in the setting of learning from human demonstrations is important."

Benchmark papers attacked for lacking method novelty: **ICLR 2026 Sub 1602 (Real-IKEA)** — https://openreview.net/forum?id=eQ4kdm5iYj [VERIFIED]: *"The major weakness is the lack of technical contribution. The authors have made a huge amount of efforts in building the benchmark. However, the technical contribution is weak."*

Also [VERIFIED]: ICLR 2025 metareview https://openreview.net/forum?id=uaKBM9sGEm (*"not well-evidenced just from simulation results (no hardware experiments were conducted)"*); ICLR 2024 Sub 5759 https://openreview.net/forum?id=UulwvAU1W0 (*"There are no real robot experiments."*, rating **"5: marginally below the acceptance threshold"**).

### 1.4 The "analysis paper" reviewer frame (generic, incl. a probing paper)

All [VERIFIED]. These are non-robotics but show the exact reviewer vocabulary:
- ICLR 2025 Sub 10771, **a probing paper**: *"W1. This paper can be considered as an analysis paper. In other words, this paper does not propose a novel idea for advancing NCO models."* — https://openreview.net/forum?id=agEy9hliY1
- ICLR 2024 Sub 7272: *"**As an analysis paper, we should try to make sure the comparisons are made under the SOTA performance**, otherwise, it would be less helpful."* — https://openreview.net/forum?id=Mm3TSPRUKc
- ICLR 2025 Sub 11679: *"I would consider this as an analysis paper. However, many of the conclusions appear somewhat obvious."* — https://openreview.net/forum?id=bSq0XGS3kW
- **Counterweight**, ICLR 2024 Sub 7917: *"However it does not seem to attack the core of the problem... **But as an analysis paper this may not be a critical weakness.**"* — https://openreview.net/forum?id=VrHiF2hsrm

### 1.5 Frequency calibration [VERIFIED counts from the search endpoint]

Exact-phrase corpus-wide hits: `"no real-robot experiments"` **18**; `"no hardware experiments"` **6** (4 of them CoRL 2024); `"no closed-loop"` **27** (heavily ICLR 2026); `"as an analysis paper"` **15**; `"does not propose a new method"` **17**; `"no new method is proposed"` **8**; `"lacks a novel method"` **2** (both EMNLP). Phrases returning **zero**: `"only offline metrics"`, `"offline metrics only"`, `"only offline evaluation"`, `"purely an analysis paper"`, `"not state-of-the-art"`, `"does not achieve state-of-the-art"`.

**Interpretation:** the anti-analysis vocabulary is real and concentrated in AC decisions at CoRL and reviewer weakness lists at ICLR, but it is **not a large absolute volume**, and reviewers attack *offline-only evaluation* by describing it ("no closed-loop", "offline metrics don't establish...") rather than by a stock phrase. Nobody writes "not SOTA" as a rejection reason in so many words.

## 3. Venue policies that help (or hurt) analysis papers

**CoRL 2026 CFP** — https://www.corl.org/contributions/call-for-papers [VERIFIED]. The pivotal sentence is **encouragement, not a requirement**:
&gt; "Authors are encouraged to report real-robot experiments or provide convincing evidence that simulation experiments are transferable to real robots."

Two adjacent points matter: **"Benchmarks and datasets for robot learning"** is a named welcomed area, and **"Submissions without a robotics focus will be returned without review."** Also mandatory Limitations section. Note the gap between this soft written policy and §1.2's AC behavior — **the norm is stricter than the rule.**

**RSS 2025 CFP** — https://roboticsconference.org/2025/information/cfp/ [VERIFIED]. Opposite posture from CoRL, novelty is criterion #1:
&gt; "Paper submissions will be evaluated in terms of their novelty, technical quality, significance, potential impact, and clarity."

RSS 2025 desk-reject list (https://roboticsconference.org/2025/reviewps/) is purely procedural — missing Limitations section, formatting, anonymization, out of scope. **RSS reviews are not public**, so no RSS review text is obtainable. **[UNVERIFIED]** I found no RSS or CoRL "position paper"/"blue sky" track for 2025/2026; CoRL 2021 did have a `Blue_Sky` OpenReview group (`robot-learning.org/CoRL/2021/Conference/Blue_Sky`) but I could not retrieve its call wording (blocked endpoints).

**TMLR acceptance criteria** — https://jmlr.org/tmlr/acceptance-criteria.html [VERIFIED, fetched via curl]. The single most favorable policy in the field:
&gt; "Crucially, it should not be used as a reason to reject work that isn't considered 'significant' or 'impactful' because it isn't achieving a new state-of-the-art on some benchmark. Nor should it form the basis for rejecting work on a method considered not 'novel enough', as **novelty of the studied method is not a necessary criterion for acceptance in TMLR**. We explicitly avoid these terms ('significant', 'impactful', 'novel')."

Also: gaps between claims and evidence may be fixed by *"authors adjust (reduce) their claims"*, not only more experiments; and *"a proper reproducibility report that systematically studies the robustness or generalizability of a published method and lays out actionable lessons for its audience could satisfy this criterion."*

**NeurIPS 2025 Reviewer Guidelines** — https://neurips.cc/Conferences/2025/ReviewerGuidelines [VERIFIED]. Directly protective:
&gt; "**originality does not necessarily require introducing an entirely new method.** Rather, a work that provides novel insights by evaluating existing methods, or demonstrates improved efficiency, fairness, etc. is also equally valuable."

**NeurIPS 2025 Datasets &amp; Benchmarks CFP** — https://neurips.cc/Conferences/2025/CallForDatasetsBenchmarks [VERIFIED]. In-scope list includes *"In-depth analyses of machine learning challenges and competitions ... that yield important new insight"*, *"Systematic analyses of existing systems on novel datasets yielding important new insight"*, and *"identifying significant problems with existing datasets and their use"*. Caveat on the same page: *"we aim for an equally stringent review as in the main conference track."* Single-blind allowed; Croissant metadata and executable code **required** (non-compliance = desk reject).

**ICML Position Paper Track** — https://icml.cc/Conferences/2025/CallForPositionPapers [VERIFIED]:
&gt; "Submissions to the main ICML conference track emphasize original research and novel results. **In contrast, submissions to the position paper track will be judged primarily on whether they present a compelling position that warrants greater exposure** within the machine learning community (regardless of whether a reviewer agrees with the position)."

Accepted position papers go **into the proceedings**. NeurIPS also runs a Position Paper Track ([VERIFIED] — I hit live `NeurIPS.cc/2025/Position_Paper_Track/...` review invitations in the corpus).

**ICLR Blogposts Track** — https://iclr-blogposts.github.io/2026/call/ [VERIFIED, 2025 and 2026 wording identical]. Explicitly invites:
&gt; "Review past work and summarize the outcomes, develop new intuitions, or **highlight some shortcomings**." ... "**Cool research ideas that you tried but did not work out**"

2025 edition: **96 submissions, 48 accepted**, double-blind, poster at the main session. Non-archival. Constraint: *"Blog Posts must not be used to highlight or advertise past publications of the authors or of their lab."*

**Negative-results / diagnosis workshops (CoRL 2026)** — all [VERIFIED]:
- **"Oops, I Erred" — Collecting, Curating and Using Imperfect Data for Realistic Scenarios**, https://workshop.oopsie-data.com/ (OpenReview group `robot-learning.org/CoRL/2026/Workshop/Oopsie`). Entirely about failure data: *"This workshop is about other data: execution failures and near-misses, noisy or suboptimal demonstrations, out-of-distribution events, and the unexpected things people do around robots. Every lab produces it, and almost none of it is documented, shared, or reused."* Faculty advisors **Peter Stone, Sergey Levine, Roberto Martín-Martín, Amy Zhang**. Offers *"an award for the most hilarious failure."*
- **SimBench2Real**, https://corl2026-realworld-robot-learning.github.io/, has a section titled **"Beyond Binary Success: Diagnostic Evaluation"**: *"Task completion alone is not enough. Stage-level metrics ... reveal precisely where and why policies fail, enabling targeted improvement rather than opaque leaderboard scores."*
- CoRL 2026 also lists workshops **"Beyond Binary Success: Diagnosing Fine-Grained Capabilities in Robot Manipulation"** and **"Do Robots Need World Models? A Debate"** ([VERIFIED] on https://www.corl.org/program/workshops).
- **RoboSoft 2026**: "Towards Reproducibility in Soft Robotics: Addressing Concerns in Manufacturing, Testing, and Simulation", https://softrobotics-mts.github.io.
- **NeurIPS ICBINB** ("I Can't Believe It's Not Better") exists as an OpenReview venue (`NeurIPS.cc/2023/Workshop/ICBINB`) [VERIFIED it exists]; **I did not retrieve its call wording** — [UNVERIFIED].

OpenReview / DBLP / PMLR 从我这里都连不通（arXiv 可以）。所以下面有一处我要标清楚：那个"同一篇 offline-only 论文被 ICLR 拒、几个月后被 ICML 收"的案例，**论文本身我核实了**（arXiv 2411.04434，`Scaling Laws for Pre-training Agents and World Models`，2024-11-07），但**两个会议的归属我没能独立复核**，是子调研从 OpenReview 拿到的。当作强线索，不当作铁证。

六份调研回来了（还有一份最关键的在跑，见最后）。我把它们整合成一张图，不再罗列。

---

# 一、领域的真实形状

**四类"世界模型"，门槛差五个数量级，中间是空的：**

| 类别 | 推理期角色 | 门槛 | 你的机会 |
|---|---|---|---|
1. 通用生成式模拟器 | 就是产品 | 2048×GB200 / 1024 TPU-v5p | **零** |
2. **小域专用世界模型** | rollout 训策略 | **单 H200 18h / 2×A100** | **有，且在真机上打赢了 Cosmos** |
3. **表征预训练 pretext**（WoG 在此） | **完全不用** | frozen ckpt 即可分析 | **最强** |
4. 评测 / 诊断 | 当 judge | 算力花在推理 | **有，且是公认痛点** |

我第一条消息说"类别 1 不能做，这是 scaling 竞赛"——**错在把整个类别 1 判死**。低峰的 Interactive World Simulator（176MB 模型，单卡 18 小时）长时程预测超过 Cosmos / Dreamer4，100% 用世界模型数据训的策略 ≈ 真实数据（87.9% vs 88.8%）。

# 二、两条主流线的病是同一个

这是六份调研自己收敛出来的，不是我的观点：

```
原始像素未来帧 ←──────────────────────→ 极度压缩的 latent action
(VPP / 视频 WAM)                              (LAPA / VQ)
      │                                            │
 不压缩时不知道该学什么                      压缩时不知道该丢什么
 → 容量花在无关视觉细节                     → 丢细粒度、留 exogenous 噪声
                          │
                    同一个病：
              监督目标与「控制相关性」不对齐
```

**而 2026 下半年的收敛答案是"在 latent 空间预测未来状态"——正是 WoG 那条线的落点。** 你押的方向没错，且现在正在变成主战场。

两条独立证据链锁死了同一个命题：
- **Prediction over Reconstruction**（2026-06）：*"strong pixel decoding quality can exhibit **near-zero action recoverability**"*
- **LARY**（美团，1.2M 样本）：三个旗舰 embodied LAM 全在 18–21 分，而**零动作监督的 V-JEPA 2 是 76.62——3.8 倍**

# 三、领域进入清算期，这是可验证的事实

四个月内，审计/负面/元研究论文的密度：

| 时间 | 工作 | 干了什么 |
|---|---|---|
2026-05 | Why Latent Actions Fail | 理论化 future leakage |
2026-06 | Prediction over Reconstruction | 像素质量 ⊥ 动作可恢复性 |
2026-06 | **How Should WM Be Evaluated**（position） | 命名 **claim/evidence mismatch**，提 L0–L7 阶梯 |
2026-07 | **What a World Model Represents Is Three Questions** | **证明 loss-ablation 无法识别模型实际使用的路径** |
2026-08 | What Matters for Latent Actions | 41 个设计选择，否定光流路线 |
2026-08 | **WorldEcho** | 现有 WM"能执行专家动作，但忽略 off-expert 轨迹" |
2026-08 | **The Intervention Gap in Latent World Models** | 用已发布 TD-MPC2 ckpt 做匹配干预审计 |
**2026-09-14** | **Reconstructing Is Not Acting** | **直接反驳 8 月那篇的 proxy metric 结论** |

最后两篇相隔 25 天、结论冲突，**这是一个敞开的裁决位**。而 CoRL 2026 有三个 workshop 专门征集这类工作（`Do Robots Need World Models?` 的六条辩论动议、`Everything Beneath the Policy`、`Beyond Binary Success`）。

# 四、发表现实：杀手不是"没 SOTA"

这是六份调研里最反直觉、也最有用的一条。OpenReview 全库精确短语命中：

| 短语 | 次数 |
|---|---|
`"no closed-loop"` | **27**（ICLR 2026 集中） |
`"does not propose a new method"` | 17 |
`"no real-robot experiments"` | 18 |
`"as an analysis paper"` | 15 |
`"findings are not particularly surprising"` | **9** |
`"not state-of-the-art"` / `"does not achieve state-of-the-art"` | **0** |

**没人把"不是 SOTA"写成拒稿理由。真正的死法是"结论不意外"**：

> **"Trivial and Unsurprising Findings**: The paper's primary conclusions are not new knowledge. The findings that later layers in a transformer are more task-specific… are foundational and well-documented"

**这条无法用更多算力解决。** 所以有一条纪律必须在动手前立：**如果结果落在符合直觉的那一边，这篇论文还有价值吗？答案是"没有"就换题。**

三条制度性出口（全部逐字核实）：
- **TMLR**：*"novelty of the studied method is **not a necessary criterion** for acceptance"*，且明说系统研究已有方法鲁棒性并给 actionable lessons 可收。**正经期刊，不是 workshop。**
- **NeurIPS 审稿指南**：*"originality does not necessarily require introducing an entirely new method"*
- **CoRL `Everything Beneath the Policy`**：*"not on state-of-the-art task performance"*，明征 negative results。**10-09 截止，4 页，只剩 24 天。**

# 五、你的位置：一个别人做不了的交集

盘完六份调研，我找到了**没人占住、而你恰好能做**的位置。它由三个条件的交集定义：

**条件一：类别 3（pretext task）的机制分析是空白。**
所有 probing 工作都做在两类对象上——VLA 策略（OpenVLA、π0、GR00T）或视频世界模型当模拟器。**"世界模型当辅助目标"这条线的两阶段 teacher/student 结构，没有人审计过。**

**条件二：这需要同时拿到 Stage-I 和 Stage-II 的 checkpoint。**
几乎没有工作会同时放出预训练两个阶段的权重。**WoG 放了，你两个都下了（61GB 在本地）。** 这是你最值钱的资产，比 OXE 数据更稀缺。

**条件三：你已经做出了一个"不意外性"过关的结果。**

> Stage-I 的 DiT 对 `O^c` 的因果作用 **96%~108% 来自未来成分**（跨 fractal/bridge）
> 但 Stage-II 对齐搬进 `z` 的，**当前帧成分比未来成分多 1.35:1**
> **而部署模型只保留了 Stage-II 的产物**

**两个阶段在用同一个 16×32 瓶颈的不同部分，而生效的那一半正好搬的是对动作无因果作用的信息。** 这个结论不符合任何人的直觉，包括原作者——它还顺带解释了论文 Table 8 自己那个被绕过去的反常（Stage-I 单独 −1.7%，全部 +16.7% 来自 Stage-II）。

**而且你用的手法正是自驾领域最成功的审计模板。** `Is Ego Status All You Need?`（CVPR 2024，已核实）第 4 步是"图像全置空，planning 几乎不变"；你的"抹掉未来（0.560）≈ 整体置零（0.582）"是同一个手法。**你在无意识地复用你老本行的模板，而具身领域还没人系统用过它。**

# 六、两个必须正视的硬约束

**约束一：PPU 无 Vulkan 切断了贵的那一半。**

```
fractal/bridge（WoG 真实训练分布，你有 235G）──► 只能 offline
LIBERO/MuJoCo EGL（能闭环 rollout）──────────► 但不是 WoG 的分布
                      ↑ 这两头对不上，别假设能都占
```

唯一合法出路（有先例）：**把 offline 指标与下游性能的相关性本身做成贡献**，让它成为被验证的代理量，而不是当性能证据。

**约束二：那篇 2026-07 的论文直接威胁你的方法。**
`What a World Model Represents Is Three Questions` 论证 **loss-ablation 无法识别模型实际使用的路径**。你 doc 10 的 exp09 正是 loss-based（比 flow loss），而且你自己已经发现它失灵了（`rand_proj` 比真实 `O^c` 还好）。**你踩的坑有论文解释，而这反而是好事——你可以引它来说明为什么必须用因果干预而非 loss ablation。**

另外一条会打死你的审稿意见，提前防：**「能力缺失」和「表征错配/readout 失败」必须分开**（反例：Feature Token Modulation 只用 4K 参数把视角准确率 48.5%→87.1%）。你 doc 09 里那句"probe 只能说明信息在不在，不能说明 action head 用没用"就是这个区分——**保住它**。

---

# 七、还有一路没回

**唯一还在跑的是 WM-as-pretext-task 完整谱系那一路**——也就是 WoG 所在的那条线。它要回答的问题里有一个是决定性的：**有没有人已经做过这个分析、你的结果是否已被抢发。** 这一路回来之前，上面第五节的"空白"判断只能算强推测，不能算结论。

投的话，**素材已经够了**，不需要新实验——最多补一个 bridge 上的 CCA 交叉验证（你 doc 12 自己标了这条局限）。4 页的篇幅正好逼你把 claim 收窄到"关于这些 checkpoint 的表征结构"，而这恰恰是审稿最保护的写法。10-26 出结果，拿到的是社区反馈 + 一个 credential，然后再用几个月做 TMLR 的完整版（加上"提纯对齐目标"那个修复）。

不投的话，我们按 TMLR 节奏铺开，把摊子做大，风险更低但周期长。

### ASSISTANT — 2026-09-15 18:07

明白。放弃 deadline，不谈投稿。下面只谈这条线本身。

## 这条线真正在问什么

WoG、latent action、VPP、JEPA 都是同一个问题的不同答案：

> **为了行动，应该在什么空间里预测未来？**

没人有原则性答案，全是经验性答案。这个问题拆成三层：

1. 这个空间**必须包含**什么（充分性）
2. 必须**排除**什么（纯度）
3. **谁来定义它** ← 关键

第 3 层是 WoG 的结构性缺口：`O^c` 的空间由 Stage-I 冻结的 `qformer` 定义，而 `qformer` 是靠"对齐未来视觉特征"训出来的——**不是靠"对动作有用"训出来的**。**定义这个空间的目标，和这个空间服务的目标，不是同一个。**

你的测量已经把这个缺口量化了：41.5% 的方差 DiT 根本不用，而 Stage-II 的梯度主要在搬那一部分。

## 所以下一个该问的

不是"再 probe 一遍 `O^c` 里有什么"，而是：

> **"对动作真正有用的未来信息"，内在维度是多少？**

WoG 选了 16×32 = 512 个数。你测出有效秩只有 18，且 16 个 query 高度冗余（单 token 0.62 vs 全 16 个 0.645）。**如果因果有效的部分其实只有个位数维度，那"该在什么空间预测未来"就有了一个定量答案**——而且是对整条线的答案，不只是对 WoG 的。

这个问题的性质是对的：不需要训练、不追指标、直接切核心。

## 第一步怎么做

复用你 exp07 的干预框架（固定初始噪声与 `z`，只换 `O^c`，测动作变化幅度），但**不再替换成 static/shuffled，而是沿主成分方向逐维消融**，画出"保留前 k 维 → 动作保真度"的曲线。

**动手前先读两处，别跳过**：
- `action_model/models.py:149-158` —— `per_attn` 怎么消费 `O^c`（它作 K/V，动作 token 作 Q）
- `vla/qformer.py:21` —— `v_proj` 投到 32 维那一步

**为什么读**：你要先确定干预点在 `v_proj` 之后还是之前。这决定你测的是"32 维输出空间"的维度，还是"16 个 query"的维度——**两者含义完全不同**，选错了整条曲线的解释就变了。

**自检项**（这条必须有）：全维度消融的扰动幅度，应该等于你已经测过的 `zeros` 那个数 **0.582**。对不上就是干预实现有 bug，先别看曲线。

---

一个岔路口，你选：

**A. 先攻"维度"**——上面这条，便宜、干净、能很快出结论。
**B. 先攻"谁定义空间"**——更根本：如果 condition space 改由"对动作有用"来定义，它会长成什么样？但这个要训东西。

我建议 A 先做，因为它的结果会直接告诉你 B 值不值得做（如果有效维度就 5 维，B 的空间就很大；如果是 18 维且分布均匀，B 的收益就有限）。

# 「未来预测作为 VLA 辅助目标」技术路线 · 2026-09 现状调研

**方法说明**：所有 arXiv 编号/日期/作者/摘要均由我或子代理直接 `curl arxiv.org/abs/&lt;id&gt;` 一手核实。凡标 **未能证实** 者为检索空缺或仅二手来源。WebFetch 对 arxiv.org 被企业策略拦截，全程走 curl。

## 0. 一句话结论

**这条线在 2026 年已经完成了「被证伪 → 被重构 → 被划定边界」三轮洗牌，而它最该做的那个对照实验（打乱未来目标）在 VLA 领域几乎无人做过。** 你 `WoG_v2/docs/07` 里从 Table 8 读出的那个反常，2026-03 之后已经成了整条线的公共议题——但**没有人用你 `wm_probe` 那种设计去回答它**。

## 1. 完整谱系图（按「预测什么空间」分类）

先给一个比「有没有 world model」更有用的切分轴——**推理时预测通路还剩多少**：

| 范式 | 定义 | 代表 |
|---|---|---|
| **A. 纯辅助（decoder 完全丢弃）** | 预测头训练时用、推理时删 | DreamVLA、FLARE、GR00T-N1.5、Seer、GR-1/GR-2、UniVLA-BAAI、**WoG** |
| **B. 单步 latent 前向**（跑但不解码像素） | 预测网络前向一次只取中间特征 | VPP、GE-Act、MinD、DiT4DiT |
| **C. 统一生成模型**（同权重可切换） | policy 模式跳过视觉分支 | UVA、WorldVLA、GigaBrain-0.5M* |
| **D. 真 rollout** | 生成未来帧 → IDM 抽动作 | UniPi、SuSIE、RoboDreamer、Vidar |

你关心的是 A（+ 部分 B）。下面按预测空间分类。

## 2. 2026-03 至今的新进展（重点：5 月后）

### ⭐ 2.1 Fast-WAM：这条线的判决性实验

**[2603.16666](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.16666)**，2026-03-17，清华 IIIS + Galaxea AI（Tianyuan Yuan, Zibin Dong, Yicheng Liu, Hang Zhao）。**标题就是你的问题**：*Do World Action Models Need Test-time Future Imagination?*

同架构四变体受控对比（Wan2.2-5B，无 embodied pretraining）：

| 变体 | 推理时生成未来 | RoboTwin | LIBERO |
|---|---|---|---|
| Fast-WAM（保留 co-train，推理不生成） | 否 | **91.8** | **97.6** |
| Fast-WAM-Joint | 是 | 90.6 | 98.5 |
| Fast-WAM-IDM | 是 | 91.3 | 98.0 |
| **去掉 video co-training** | 否 | **83.8** | **93.5** |

&gt; "the main value of video prediction in WAMs may lie in improving world representations **during training** rather than generating future observations at test time."

延迟 190ms，比 imagine-then-execute 快 4×。**这直接为「推理时不 rollout」这条路线提供了正当性**，也是 5 月后几乎所有论文的引用锚点。

### ⭐ 2.2 OpenWAM：唯一的 scaling + 统一 codebase

**[2609.07398](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.07398)**，**2026-09-07**（北大 Hao Dong / 清华 Hang Zhao / NUS 等 24 作者），代码 github.com/OpenWAM-Official/OpenWAM。518.5M 帧 / ≈6400 小时预训练。三个对你极重要的结论：

1. **纯辅助不够**：attention mask 消融（RoboTwin2.0-Full）——Isolated（两流隔离）**87.41** vs Action-Sees-Video **92.39** vs Mutual 92.15。**光共享 backbone 加辅助头，比让 action 能读 world 特征低约 5 点。**
2. **独立复现 Fast-WAM**：扫遍异步去噪 schedule，**同步最佳**，原文说这"supports the **representation learning hypothesis** ... as opposed to an implicit planning-then-IDM schedule at test time"。
3. **规模改变最优设计（偏好反转）**：from scratch 时偏好单向轻耦合（Action-Sees-Video 比 Mutual 好 0.24pp），预训练后翻转为偏好 Mutual（+0.16pp）。且 embodied pretraining 收益 **OOD +12.12pp vs ID 仅 +0.68pp**。
4. **ID/OOD 分岔**：WAM 在 ID 更会拟合（video-latent 项注入额外信息源），但 **LIBERO-Plus 上 VLA 反超**——"长 horizon 预测在分布偏移下意味着更重的误差累积"。

### 2.3 边界条件：LAWA 的反击

**[2608.24882](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.24882)**，2026-08-25。摘要原文：
&gt; "our **matched implementations** show **lower generalization for Fast-WAM** than for future-aware alternatives, **especially with scarce robot demonstrations and in out-of-distribution scenarios**."

RoboCasa few-shot 65.6% / full 80.8%，比 matched Fast-WAM +9.6 / +4.5。结论句 "**future imagination need not be discarded**"。

**综合 Fast-WAM + OpenWAM + LAWA + FOCA（[2606.20867](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.20867)，ICML 2026，增益集中在 20 条示范的 few-shot 区间）→ 目前这条线最清晰的边界：「丢弃论」在数据充足 + ID 下成立，在数据稀缺 + OOD 下不成立。**

### 2.4 两家巨头都放弃了（⚠️ 最重要的趋势信号，我亲自核实）

- **ByteDance：GR-1(像素) → GR-2(VQ token) → GR-3 完全砍掉。** 我对 GR-3 全文（[2507.15493](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.15493)）做了 grep：`video prediction` / `world model` / `GR-2` **各仅 1 次命中，且全部在参考文献里**；`future frame` / `future image` **0 次**。总损失只有 flow-matching + next-token；唯一辅助监督是把 "task status"（Ongoing/Terminated/Invalid）**当额外动作维度**——一个标量，不是 world modeling。
- **NVIDIA：N1 无 → N1.5 加 FLARE → N1.6/N1.7 移除。** N1.5 **无 arXiv 论文**，唯一权威源是 [research.nvidia.com/labs/gear/gr00t-n1_5](https://research.nvidia.com/labs/gear/gr00t-n1_5/)（λ=0.2）。⚠️ **公开代码里 FLARE 是死代码**：`flow_matching_action_head.py` 有 `future_tokens` 但 `return_all_hidden_states=False,  # NOTE (YL): not using flare now`，且不存在投影 MLP / cosine loss。N1.7 源码里 `future_tokens` 彻底消失。
- **π₀.₅**：我 grep 了 [2504.16054](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.16054) 正文（去掉参考文献，59k 字符）——`future frame`/`future image`/`video prediction`/`world model`/`auxiliary` **全部 0 命中**。

**即：两家最有真机部署压力的团队，在最新一代都不用这个目标。** 但注意各家原因可能不同（GR-3 转向 π0 式 VL co-train；N1.6+ 转向更强 VLM + 更多人类视频），**因果解读未能证实**。

### 2.5 综述与 2026 新趋势

**World Models for Robotic Manipulation: A Survey [2606.00113](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.00113)**（2026-05-27，港大 Jia Pan 等）——你 `wm_probe/exp/fig_design.py` 引的就是它。它的三问框架（预测什么表征 / 怎么连到 action / 在 pipeline 哪个阶段用）正是本调研的骨架，且**明确把你的问题点为核心难题**：

&gt; "The central difficulty in downstream evaluation is **attribution**. If a world-model-augmented policy outperforms a baseline, the gain may come from better representations, additional imagined data, auxiliary prediction losses, test-time search, reward shaping, or a combination... **Without such ablations, task success alone cannot reveal how prediction helped.**"

以及对 A 类的定性批评：
&gt; "Unless the predictive pathway is carefully exposed or ablated, improved performance may reflect **better representation learning rather than reliable online reasoning**."

其他：World Action Models: A Survey [2606.20781](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.20781)（NUS，57 页，判断句 "The field is moving toward methods that **generate less of the future while preserving what control requires**"）· [2605.12090](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.12090)（复旦）· [2605.00080](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.00080)（含 Abbeel/Malik/Jiajun Wu，43 页，Table 6 有一列就叫 "Future Generation at Inference"）· **[2606.15032](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.15032)**（南大，position paper，直指 **claim/evidence mismatch**，提 L0–L7 证据阶梯）· **[2606.30686](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.30686)**（Position: VLA 的物理推理**不可检验**，指出 **narrative drift**）

**2026 三个新趋势**：① 预测目标从像素→latent→**「只预测控制需要的那一小块」**（mask / 腕部 / 自身关键点 / 力矩）；② 「training-only，推理零成本」成为显式卖点；③ 出现**竞争性替代假设**——VLAct [2608.27550](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.27550) 走「别把预训练表征洗掉」，在 RoboDojo 上**超过所有 WAM 条目**，且只用 16 GPU。

## 3. 公开批评与争议

### ⭐ 3.1 最强否证来自 RL 领域，且这条线基本没引用

**"Does Self-supervised Learning Really Improve Reinforcement Learning from Pixels?"** [2206.05266](https://arxiv.org/abs/2206.05266)，**NeurIPS 2022**（Li, Shang, Das, Ryoo）。我已核实摘要原文：

&gt; "the existing SSL framework for RL **fails to bring meaningful improvement over the baselines only taking advantage of image augmentation** when the same amount of data and augmentation is used."

它测了 19 种自监督损失 × 10 seeds，其中有一整类叫 **"RL Context Prediction"**，包含 `Predict-Future` / `Guess-Future`——即世界模型辅助目标的最小形式。DMControl Relative Score：

| 方法 | 得分 |
|---|---|
| **DrQ（无任何辅助损失，只有数据增强）** | **6.028** |
| CURL | 1.128 |
| **Predict-Future（预测未来状态）** | **−6.201** |
| **Guess-Future** | **−7.318** |

**预测未来是 19 个损失里倒数第二、第三，比不做数据增强还差。** 配套：DrQ [2004.13649](https://arxiv.org/abs/2004.13649) 摘要明写 "**without the need for auxiliary losses or pre-training**"；RAD [2004.14990](https://arxiv.org/abs/2004.14990)；CURL [2004.04136](https://arxiv.org/abs/2004.04136)。

⚠️ **诚实限定**：CURL 作者反驳"RAD 只优化奖励，对比目标在稀疏奖励下才有价值"。VLA 是稠密监督的模仿学习，更接近 DMControl，但你应主动承认这个 gap。

### 3.2 这条线自己的数据就不支持「目标语义重要」（最强论辩位置）

四个数据点**全部出自原作者**：

| 论文 | 证据 |
|---|---|
| **GR-1** Table 5 | 预测步长 1/3/5 → 3.61/3.82/3.67（**波动仅 0.21**）；而有无预测头是 3.33→3.82（**0.49**）。预测第 1 步≈当前帧复制，几乎无未来信息，仍得 3.61 ≫ 3.33 |
| **Seer** Table 3 | 微调阶段单加未来预测 **仅 +0.10**（3.31→3.41）；预训练阶段 +0.09。rebuttal 补充：**仅逆动力学 3.75 ≥ 仅未来预测 3.73** |
| **FLARE** Table 2 | 换成通用 SigLIP2（与动作无关）仍得 49.6%，**average-pooled（信息更少）反而更好 50.9%**，vs 精心设计的 action-aware 55.0%、baseline 43.9%。**通用目标吃掉 51–63% 增益** |
| **DreamVLA** rebuttal | 单独预测 **DINOv2 3.13 / SAM 3.25 / 深度 2.98，三个全部低于 vanilla 3.64**。作者原文："a pure DINO loss drives the backbone to match appearance embeddings instead of action cues, so performance drops (–0.51)" |

**DreamVLA 那条对整条线是重创**：DINO 未来特征预测正是 FLARE / DINO-WM 的核心机制，DreamVLA 在自己架构里测出它掉 0.51。

### ⭐ 3.3 shuffled-future 对照：只有一篇做过，且做的不是同一件事

**Privileged Foresight Distillation (PFD)** [2604.25859](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.25859)，2026-04-28，Southampton + Queensland。我读了全文，它三个 "epistemic probes"（LIBERO 均值）：

| 配置 | 均值 |
|---|---|
| Fast-WAM (reproduced) | 96.95 |
| Pure finetune（matched-capacity） | 96.70（**低于 baseline**） |
| **Shuffled-future PFD** | **96.62** |
| PFD (default) | **98.10** |

shuffled 定义："replaces the teacher's future frames with frames drawn from an **unrelated trajectory in the same batch**"，且 "the adapter, the loss weights, and the schedule are otherwise identical"。

**但要精确理解**：PFD 打乱的是它自己**蒸馏 residual 的 teacher 未来**，不是基础的 video co-training loss。**「把 GR-1/Seer/FLARE/WoG 的未来重建目标换成打乱目标」这个实验，在 VLA 文献中未能找到。** 我核查了主要论文：GR-1 / Seer / VPP / FLARE / DreamVLA / WorldVLA / Genie Envisioner / **WoG 全文 `shuffl` `placebo` `sanity` 各 0 次命中**。

⚠️ **一个必须避开的假线索**：[2605.29864](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.29864) 有个 `WrongFuture` 条件，但那是**推理时输入端**错配（策略以错误未来为条件，结果全 0.0），不是训练时目标端错配。**误引会被审稿人当场抓住。**

### 3.4 「增益来自额外训练」的作者自认

**DriveVLA-W0**（ICLR 2026，OpenReview `plrGn3RdzN`）—— Reviewer 问"为何 700k 数据上加 world model 反而更差"，作者回答：

&gt; "the performance dip was caused by **suboptimal convergence** due to an **insufficient training schedule** ... we **increased the training steps for the 700k dataset from 15k to 20k**. ... with adequate training, the model equipped with world modeling now surpasses the baseline."

**基线没有得到同等步数追加。** 且损失权重 α: 0→0.1 吃掉 91% 增益，之后 α 增大 10 倍几乎无变化——**阶跃而非单调，是正则化特征而非表征学习特征**。

### 3.5 审稿人怎么说

- **Seer** Reviewer tjHp（本次最重要一句）："the authors only report success rates, but **not network sizes and MACs**. It becomes unclear whether **the performance gain comes from a larger network or a better method**."
- **VPP** Reviewer xoHf（打 3 分）：Voltron ViT-Base ~83M vs SVD &amp;gt;1.5B，"**This substantial discrepancy in model scale undermines the validity of the comparison**"。作者回复实质是承认做不到："pretraining these vision encoder with billions of parameters from scratch requires enormous computational resources, **which we really can not afford**."
- **DreamVLA** Reviewer Pixv：要求"try adding each prediction **on top of the vanilla VLA**"——正是这个要求逼出了 3.2 里那组自证否定数据。
- **GR-1** Reviewer SaZc：要求对比"pre-training for video prediction vs **masked prediction, contrastive learning etc.**"，并指出基准"**saturated with 88% baseline**"。
- **DriveVLA-W0** Reviewer kyet：直接点破定位——"The proposed 'world model' is **used only as auxiliary supervision during training and not for downstream planning**, limiting its conceptual impact."

**关键观察：我抓取的全部评审中，无一人要求过 shuffled/random 目标对照。**

### 3.6 三篇独立指向「predictive 目标不自足」

- [2606.30068](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.30068) —— JEPA 目标**丢弃 exogenous 但 control-relevant 特征**，因为它优化 temporal predictability 而非 control-relevance；补救只需 2% reward 标注
- [2607.26924](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.26924) —— LeWM 目标把方差偏向 temporally persistent 成分，**压制 residual**，夹爪动力学可解码性下降；只对 residual 施加 SIGReg → LIBERO Goal ×1.66
- [2608.06799](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.06799) —— *Is Forward Prediction Enough?* 加 proprio grounding + multi-horizon 关节角变化，"applied **only during training**"

### 3.7 其他重要旁证

- **VLM4VLA** [2601.03309](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.03309)（**ICLR 2026** ✅）：在 7 个辅助具身任务上微调变强，**控制反而变差**——直接切断「辅助任务→表征→控制」链条中间环节
- **Drop-Then-Recovery**（OpenReview `eH3geJAEHX`）：LIBERO 上**砍掉一半 LLM block 反而 95.0→98.3**，说明基准对表征质量几乎不施压
- **Is Ego Status All You Need?** [2312.03031](https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.03031)（CVPR 2024）：nuScenes 73.9% 直行，纯 ego-MLP 匹敌 SOTA——驾驶域的经典类比
- **Random Teachers are Good Teachers** [2302.12091](https://arxiv.org/abs/2302.12091)（ICML 2023）：向**随机初始化**教师蒸馏，学生 probing 精度反超教师，机理是"**implicit regularization in the gradient dynamics without any dark knowledge**"——最接近「随机目标同样有效」的已证结果
- **VC-1 / CortexBench** [2303.18240](https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.18240)：**无通用最优预训练目标** · [2212.05749](https://arxiv.org/abs/2212.05749)：从零学习匹敌 PVR

## 4. 消融的空白（系统性缺失）

| 缺失项 | 现状 |
|---|---|
| **打乱/随机未来目标对照** | **仅 PFD 一篇，且打乱的是蒸馏 teacher 而非 co-training loss。基础版本无人做** |
| **参数量 / MACs 匹配** | 普遍缺失。GR-1 去掉预测头时**同时移除 [OBS] token**（减容量+减序列长）；VPP 用 1.5B SVD 比 83M Voltron |
| **训练预算匹配** | WoG 是少数做了的（附录 9.3 明写对齐 150k steps）；DriveVLA-W0 反例——只给自己加步数 |
| **vanilla baseline** | DreamVLA 靠 rebuttal 才补上，补上后三个目标全负 |
| **分离「额外 decoder 容量」与「未来信息」** | 几乎无人做。DreamVLA/FLARE 的 query token 推理时仍前向，被丢弃的只是 decoder head——**这两者从未被分开测量** |
| **匹配的非预测性辅助任务** | 普遍缺失。审稿意见反复要求"a matched non-predictive auxiliary task on the same data" |
| **误差棒 / 显著性检验** | 普遍缺失。Seer 在 rebuttal 补了 t 检验（罕见）；WoG 真机每任务 **20 试次**、SimplerEnv 24 试次，5% 差异（1 次成功）当有意义差异报告，**无 CI** |
| **多 seed** | 罕见。PFD 报了 ±std（96.95±0.08），是少数 |

**统计功效问题值得单独强调**：n=20 时 60% vs 50% 的 p≈0.53。**这个领域的常规试次预算，原理上无法区分「真实未来」与「打乱未来」。** 这既是空白，也是做这个实验必须先解决的设计约束。

## 四处设计修改（基于调研，都有理由）

**1. 加一条 `static` 臂**（复制当前帧当目标），位置在 `none` 与 `random` 之间。
理由：GR-1 的 h=1 ≈ 当前帧复制，仍得 3.61 ≫ 无头 3.33。`random` 是"无信息"，`static` 是"有信息但无未来"——**分开才能区分"正则化"与"时序信息"**。你 `WoG_v2/docs/06` 用过这招，逻辑是通的。

**2. h 轴很可能是平的，提前把这当成结果写进去。**
GR-1 的证据就是这样。"看多远无所谓"本身就是支持正则化解释的证据，不是失败。

**3. 统计功效是这个实验的生死线。**

## 我读你审计文档时发现的一个更锋利的说法

这是我想跟你聊的核心。

WoG 的 Stage I 里，`qformer` 是**可训练的**，梯度从 `act_loss` 经 `per_attn` 回流到它。所以 `O^c` 这个空间**是由"对动作有用"定义出来的**——这是 WoG 设计里真正漂亮的地方，比论文自己讲得清楚。

**但它只有充分性压力，没有纯度压力。**

`act_loss` 只逼 `O^c` **包含**有用信息，不逼它**排除**无用信息。而瓶颈是 16×32=512 维——够宽，没有压缩项，于是无用信息就留在里面了。

**这就解释了你测到的 41.5%**：那不是 bug，是目标函数的必然结果。一个信息瓶颈缺了压缩项。

然后 Stage II 出事了：`per_attn` 关掉，`O^c` 不再进 DiT，改当对齐目标塑造 `z`。于是——

> **这个空间是为一个用途定义的，却被用在另一个用途上。**
> Stage I 说"你要能被 per_attn 用"，Stage II 说"你要能被 VLM 预测"。
> 中间那 41.5% 在第一个用途里是惰性的，在第二个用途里却占了 1.35:1 的梯度份额。

**而部署模型只保留 Stage II。** 所以生效的那条路，主要在搬 Stage I 自己的优化早就判定为无用的东西。

这个说法比"两阶段错配"锋利得多，因为它**指出了原因**（缺纯度项），而不只是描述现象。而且它自带修复方向。

按上面的说法，修复应该在**目标函数**里，不在事后：给 Stage I 加一个纯度压力（`O^c` 与当前帧特征的正交约束，或者干脆一个信息惩罚项）。

## 未来帧采样不是"均匀采 4 帧"

```python
future_obs_column_indices = [0,  Ta//4,  Ta//2,  3*Ta//4,  window+Ta-1]
```

**是 5 个索引，而且第一个是 0——也就是当前帧本身。** `Ta=16` 时是 `[0, 4, 8, 12, 16]`。

所以：
- 论文说"horizon 16 内均匀采 4 帧" → 实际是 **1 个当前帧 + 4 个未来帧**
- 我之前审计写的"未来 4 帧"也不准

**这对你的分析是直接冲击**：DINO 分支吃的 5 帧里，**1/5 就是当前帧**。而 Wan VAE 分支又额外把当前帧拼在最前面。所以当前帧在 `O^c` 里被喂了**两次**。

> **你测到的 41.5% 当前帧成分，现在有了机械解释：它是被显式喂进去的，两条分支都喂。**

这比"目标函数没有纯度项"更具体——不只是"没惩罚夹带"，是**架构主动把当前帧喂了两遍**。

另外 `floored_action_chunk_indices` 做了 `tf.minimum(..., goal_timestep)` 截断：**episode 末尾时，5 个索引会塌到同一帧**。所以接近结束的样本，`O^c` 里的"未来"就是当前帧的复制。这个占比多少值得算——它可能是 41.5% 的另一部分来源。

## `obs_ins` 也搞清楚了

```python
last_hidden = last_hidden[:, num_patch:]   # 砍掉视觉 patch token
obs_ins = last_hidden[:, -4:]              # 取最后 4 个
```

先切掉视觉 patch，剩下的是文本侧序列，取**最后 4 个 token**。而 `cognition_features`（就是 `z`）是用 `attention_mask` 找到最后一个有效位置取的**那 1 个 token**。

**所以 `obs_ins` 的最后一个 token 与 `z` 高度重叠**（padding 情况下可能就是同一个）。Stage II 让 `oformer` 从这 4 个 token 预测 `O^c`，而 `z` 是其中之一——这解释了为什么 Stage II 的对齐能那么强地改变 `z`（你测到余弦 0.791）：**梯度直接落在 `z` 身上，不是间接的。**

坐实了：**`oformer` 在整个代码库里只出现两次**——第 74 行构造、第 185 行使用。`load_vla` 里没有任何加载它的分支，`all_module_keys` 里没有它，所以保存时也不收集它。

> **`oformer` 训完就丢了。** 它从不被存、从不被载。

这跟我之前说的"Stage II 的 `O^c_hat` 是彻底的旁路"是一致的，但现在更彻底：**不是"推理时不算"，是这个模块的权重根本不存在于任何 checkpoint 里。**

所以 `oformer` 唯一的作用是：**在 Stage II 训练期，充当一条把梯度从"预测 `O^c`"这个任务，导流回 VLM 的 `obs_ins`（含 `z`）上的管道。** 训完管道拆掉，只留下被它塑形过的 `z`。

这让整个架构的逻辑变得非常清楚了：

```
Stage I:  act_loss 唯一压力  →  qformer 学出 O^c 空间
          （只要求"够用"，不要求"干净"；且当前帧被喂两遍）
                    │  qformer 冻结 + detach，空间定型
                    ▼
Stage II: obs_loss 把 O^c 当固定靶子
          oformer 从 obs_ins(含 z) 去追它
          梯度回流 → 重塑 VLM 的 z          ← 唯一留下的东西
                    │  oformer 丢弃
                    ▼
部署:     O_t,L → z → DiT → A     （per_attn 权重为 0 个）
```

**整套机制的净效果是：用一个"由 act_loss 定义、但夹带了双份当前帧"的目标，去正则化 VLM 的 `z`。** 而你测到 Stage II 搬进 `z` 的当前帧成分是未来成分的 1.35 倍——**现在这不是意外，是可预期的**：靶子里当前帧本来就超配。

# 探索结果：整套机制现在是闭合的

四个疑点我都查掉了，其中**两个推翻了原有认知**。

## 1. Stage I 只有 `act_loss`（证实，且比我说的更干净）

```python
if self.train_venc:                      # Stage I
    obs_loss = torch.zeros_like(act_loss)     # ← 硬置零
```

`qformer` 无条件构造、仅 Stage II 冻结。所以 **`O^c` 这个空间完全由"对动作生成有用"定义出来**，没有重建项、没有对齐项、**没有压缩项**。

→ 41.5% 惰性方差是目标函数的必然产物：`act_loss` 奖励"包含有用信息"，对"夹带无用信息"零惩罚，而 512 维瓶颈够宽。

## 2. ⚠️ 未来帧采样不是"均匀 4 帧"（推翻论文 + 推翻我之前的审计）

```python
future_obs_column_indices = [0, Ta//4, Ta//2, 3*Ta//4, window+Ta-1]
# Ta=16 → [0, 4, 8, 12, 16]
```

**5 个索引，第一个是 0 = 当前帧。** 所以 DINO 分支吃的 5 帧里 1/5 是当前帧，而 Wan VAE 分支**又**把当前帧拼在最前面。

> **当前帧被喂了两次。你测到的 41.5%，现在有机械解释了。**

另外 `floored_action_chunk_indices` 做了 `tf.minimum(..., goal_timestep)` 截断 → **episode 末尾时 5 个索引塌到同一帧**，"未来"退化成当前帧复制。这可能是 41.5% 的第二个来源，且可以算出占比。

## 3. `obs_ins` 与 `z` 高度重叠（解释了 Stage II 为何那么有力）

```python
last_hidden = last_hidden[:, num_patch:]   # 切掉视觉 patch
obs_ins = last_hidden[:, -4:]              # 最后 4 个 token
# 而 z = 用 attention_mask 找到的最后一个有效 token
```

**`z` 就在 `obs_ins` 这 4 个里面。** 所以 Stage II 的梯度**直接落在 `z` 上**，不是间接影响——这解释了你测到的余弦 0.791（"不是微调，是实质性重塑"）。

## 4. `oformer` 训完就丢

全代码库只出现两次（构造、使用）。`all_module_keys` 里没有它，`load_vla` 里没有加载分支。**它的权重不存在于任何 checkpoint。**

→ `oformer` 唯一作用是**训练期的一条梯度导流管**：把"预测 `O^c`"的梯度导回 VLM 的 `obs_ins`（含 `z`）。训完拆管，只留被塑形的 `z`。

# 整套机制（现在闭合了）

```
Stage I   act_loss 是唯一压力 → qformer 学出 O^c
          ⚠️ 只要「够用」不要「干净」；当前帧被喂两遍
                    │ qformer 冻结 + detach，空间定型
                    ▼
Stage II  O^c 当固定靶子，oformer 从 obs_ins(含 z) 去追
          梯度直落 z → 重塑 VLM 表征        ← 唯一留下的
                    │ oformer 丢弃
                    ▼
部署      O_t,L → z → DiT → A      （per_attn 权重 0 个）
```

**净效果：用一个"由 act_loss 定义、但夹带双份当前帧"的目标，正则化 VLM 的 `z`。**

你测到"Stage II 搬进 `z` 的当前帧成分 : 未来成分 = 1.35 : 1"——**现在这不是意外，是可预期的**：靶子里当前帧本来就超配。

---

# 这把 idea 变成了什么

之前的说法是"两阶段错配"（描述现象）。现在可以说成：

> **WoG 的 condition space 由动作有用性定义，但架构把当前帧喂了两遍、目标函数又没有纯度项。于是这个瓶颈里超配了当前帧信息。Stage-I 的 DiT 会忽略它（惰性 41.5%），但 Stage-II 的对齐无法忽略——它只能整体去追这个靶子，于是 1.35:1 的梯度预算花在 VLM 本来就看得见的信息上。而部署模型只保留 Stage-II 的产物。**

这个版本有三个好处：**有代码依据、指出了机制原因（不只是现象）、自带修复方向**（去掉索引 0 / 加正交约束 / 排除末尾截断样本）。

而且**最便宜的那个修复几乎是免费的**：`future_obs_column_indices` 里那个 `0` 去掉，换成 `Ta//5` 之类。这是一行改动，但它改变的是靶子本身的成分——**比你 `docs/10` 的事后 purify 更根本，而且不会造成分布外输入**（因为 `qformer` 会重新学）。

现在这个问题有了一个清晰的一般形式，而且**两条线的病正好是镜像的**：

| | 压缩压力 | 结果 |

**共同的缺失是同一个东西：两者都只约束了信息的"量"，没约束信息的"类型"。**

- WoG 有"充分性压力"（`act_loss` 逼它够用）但无"纯度压力"
- LAM 有"容量压力"（瓶颈逼它压缩）但无"方向压力"——没人告诉它该优先丢什么

WoG 的答案是"下游有用就行"（充分性），LAM 的答案是"压到很小就行"（容量）。**两者都没有直接约束"排除什么"。**

# 一、CVPR 改变了什么

这是最重要的一点，抛开具体 idea 先说：

**你的所有硬约束，在 CVPR 下基本不构成问题。**

| 约束 | CoRL / ICLR-robotics | CVPR |
|---|---|---|
没有真机 | `"no real-robot experiments"` 命中 18 次，AC 直接卡 | 不要求 |
不能闭环 rollout | `"no closed-loop"` 命中 27 次 | 不要求 |
PPU 无 Vulkan | 切断 SAPIEN/SIMPLER | **完全无影响**——视频世界模型是纯 PyTorch，不需要渲染器 |
单卡 | 拼不过 scaling | 诊断/评测类论文算力花在推理 |

**反过来，CVPR 要的东西你未必有**：它要"这是个视觉贡献"，要漂亮的定性图，要跟多个已有模型的对比表。纯机器人系统论文在 CVPR 会被打"not vision enough"。

**所以选题的判据变了**：不是"这对机器人有用吗"，而是"**这是不是一个视觉/表征的测量问题**"。

# 二、三个方向

我按"独立想"来给，不接你之前的实验。

## 方向 A：3D 一致性是那个缺失的度量

**Claim**：世界模型生成的视频逐帧看没问题，但**不对应一个物理上可实现的 3D 场景**；而 3D 不一致性比 FVD/PSNR 更能预测控制失败。

**为什么新**：现在已经有六组人独立证明了"生成质量 ⊥ 控制效用"（Physics-IQ、Prediction over Reconstruction、Dream.exe、WorldSimProbe…），但**没人给出视觉侧的解释**。大家只是反复确认相关性不存在。这个方向给出机制：缺的不是画质，是 3D 一致性。

**怎么做**：把 3D 基础模型（VGGT / DUSt3R / MonST3R）**当测量仪器**用——在世界模型的 rollout 上跑重建，测几何自一致性（重投影误差、深度时序漂移、相机轨迹可解性），再跟下游控制指标算秩相关。

**为什么很 CVPR**：用 3D 基础模型做 instrument 是 CVPR 的母语；输出天然是好图（并排放真实视频和 rollout 的重建点云）；纯推理，单卡够。

## 方向 B：接触事件锚定的诊断

**Claim**：世界模型的失败**集中在接触发生/断开的那几帧**，而现有指标在全部帧上取平均，正好把它抹掉了。按真实接触事件重新加权后，模型排序会变。

**为什么新**：WorldSimProbe（2026-08，18,000+ 实例）发现 tap 最强、pull/rotate/knock-over 弱、**shake 几乎为零（0.0–1.2）**，但它**只能用视觉指标 + VLM 判定**。没人把预测误差与**真实接触力**对齐过。

**你的独家条件**：MuJoCo 能给你精确的接触法向力、摩擦状态、滑移速度、穿透深度。**这是只有能访问物理引擎内部状态的人才能做的诊断。**

**风险**：MuJoCo 当 ground truth，结论是"世界模型能否替代一个已有仿真器"，不是"替代真实世界"。CVPR 对此比 CoRL 宽容得多，但要在写法上主动界定。

## 方向 C：把失败翻成特征

**Claim**：世界模型不懂物理，但**它的"惊讶"能定位物理事件**。

**怎么做**：冻结的世界模型，逐 patch 算预测误差 → 证明它与真实接触事件强相关（用 B 的 MuJoCo ground truth 验证）→ 然后**拿它去做点什么**（接触检测 / affordance / 关键帧提取）。

**为什么这条对 CVPR 最关键**：**它把诊断变成了方法。** CVPR 比 CoRL 更吃"新方法"。纯 benchmark 在 CVPR 也能进，但竞争激烈；"诊断 + 由诊断导出的方法"是更稳的形态。

# 三、我的建议

**主推 A，B 当 A 的验证层，C 当加分项。**

理由：
- A 的 claim 最锋利，而且它回答的是一个**已被反复确认但无人解释**的现象——这天然免疫"结论不意外"（那是拒稿真正的杀手，OpenReview 命中 9 次，而"没 SOTA"是 0 次）
- A 纯推理，两个月够
- A 完全不碰你的硬件短板
- 有了 B 的接触 ground truth，A 就从"相关性观察"升级为"有物理依据的解释"

**组合成一句话的论文**：

> 世界模型的视觉质量与控制效用无关，因为主流指标测的是逐帧外观；真正决定效用的是 3D 一致性与接触时刻的保真度，而这两者可以用现成的 3D 基础模型和物理引擎真值直接测量。

# 四、两个月的现实检查

**必须先确认的一件事**：能跑起来几个开源世界模型的 checkpoint。候选有 Cosmos-Predict、IRASim、Ctrl-World、DreamDojo 等（WorldSimProbe 评了 6 个开源 ACWM）。**没有 ≥4 个模型的对比表，CVPR 很难过。**

这是唯一的真实风险点——不是算法，是"能不能在 PPU 上把四个别人的模型跑起来"。你在 WoG 上做过一次（TF stub、权重路径、bf16 那些坑），知道代价。

**建议第一周就只做这一件事**：挑 4 个 checkpoint，验证能在 PPU 上出 rollout。跑不通就换方向，别拖到第六周才发现。

## Bottom line

**No, it is not reliable by default — and the literature now says so explicitly.** As of 2026 there is a small but real cluster of papers that directly address your question. The strongest single piece of evidence is that VGGT/DUSt3R/MASt3R/Fast3R **hallucinate dense geometry and cross-view support even on random Gaussian noise and unrelated scenes**, which means a high "3D consistency" score from a pointmap model carries no guarantee that the input was 3D-consistent at all. Meanwhile the benchmarks that use these models as instruments split into three camps: those that ignore the problem, those that acknowledge it as a limitation without measuring it, and a small number (GeCo, WorldMark, SGC) that actually calibrate a noise floor.

**Caveat on dates:** many of the most relevant papers carry 2026 arXiv IDs (26xx.xxxxx) and were verified live against arxiv.org today. The arXiv Atom API was IP-rate-limited throughout, so I verified via `curl` on `arxiv.org/abs/&lt;id&gt;`, extracting `citation_title`, `citation_date`, `citation_author`, the Comments field and submission/revision history. That is the same metadata the API returns, so I consider these VERIFIED; I note below the two items I could not verify.
